intro: Will the furniture move with the user or depend on this particular site? Classify its relationship to the room and its degree of customization before assigning design and installation responsibilities.

sections.title: Freestanding or built-in?
sections.text: Freestanding furniture has a comparatively independent form; built-in furniture relies on its relationship with the site. Neither category removes the need to review stability and fixing requirements. For built-ins, document interfaces with finishes and services, and how the unit can be removed or maintained.
sections.caption: A conceptual diagram; read it with the explanation.

sections.title: How much customization?
sections.text: Standard furniture comes with defined product specifications. Semi-custom options allow changes within a supplier’s system. Bespoke furniture is developed for the project. A dimension change does not automatically preserve joint suitability, capacity or warranty: obtain the supplier’s modification limits.
sections.caption: A conceptual diagram; read it with the explanation.

sections.title: Define interfaces and responsibilities
sections.text: Separate design, supply, fabrication, transport, installation and service coordination. State what is included and who owns external work. Identify who confirms fixing substrates and who remeasures after finishes. Each deliverable needs an owner and handover point; “all inclusive” does not define these interfaces.
sections.caption: A conceptual diagram; read it with the explanation.

example.title: Worked example
example.text: A cabinet made for a specific recess with an outlet behind it is both built-in and bespoke. The furniture package must address access and coordination, but electrical alterations are not automatically part of furniture fabrication.
example.decision: Decision: agree the scope and interfaces before issuing construction details.

options: Modifications within the supplier’s defined system
